transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-11
Start: 15:30 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alice Park (Redwood AE), Benji Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Lynx CTO), Rafael Ortiz (Lynx Lead ML Eng), Priya Singh (Lynx Platform Eng)

Auto-Summary (auto-generated, rough):
- Objective: scope a 2-week POC to validate latency/SLA and cost tradeoffs for Lynx Commerce conversational search and checkout assistant.
- Primary metrics: p95 latency under 350ms for interactive flows, sustain 120 QPS read traffic with 30 concurrent sessions, 10% tail burst to 300 QPS; token cost target <$0.0025 per query.
- Next steps: Redwood to send benchmark template + replay scripts; Lynx to share anonymized traces; schedule infra deep-dive.

Topics flagged: QPS shape, concurrency vs. cost, input/output token distribution, canary/fallback strategies, security (SOC2/KMS), timeline for pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alice Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alice from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. Benji is our solutions engineer, he'll drive the test plan details.
[00:08] Maya Chen: Hi all, Maya here. Thanks. We wanted to... uh.. scope a short pilot to understand cost & latency for our checkout assistant.
[00:15] Benji Rao: Great. Quick agenda — collect your success criteria, go over workload shape (QPS, concurrency, token mix), propose a benchmark plan and timeline. Sound okay?
[00:23] Rafael Ortiz: Yep, sounds good. Quick context — our traffic is a mix of read-only semantic search (70%) and short-form generative responses in checkout (30%). Average session length is 3–4 queries, but users sometimes do longer dialog.
[00:36] Priya Singh: Also, infra notes — we're in AWS us-east-1, VPC peering option preferable (we want to use Redwood Private). We have strict PII rules, so we'd need audit logs and KMS integration.
[00:47] Alice Park: Noted. On the PII/Security side we can surface SOC2 and our KMS pattern. We'll include runbook.
[00:52] Maya Chen: Thanks. For metrics — we care about tail latency and SLOs. p95 under 350ms for the search calls, p99 ideally under 700ms; for gen calls p95 under 600ms acceptable. Cost target is rough: under $0.0025 per interactive query averaged across traffic.
[01:10] Benji Rao: Helpful — when you say 'interactive query' are you measuring tokens per user-turn or per session?
[01:15] Rafael Ortiz: We typically measure per user-turn. Average input tokens ~40 tokens, generation ~120 tokens for the gen path, search embeddings are single-call, about 512 dims but that's separate.
[01:27] Alice Park: So token mix you're giving is input 40, output 120 for gen, and search is mostly embedding and rerank?
[01:33] Rafael Ortiz: Rerank is a small piece, yes. Search path: hitting embedding model then a cheap reranker, so token cost there is negligible compared to the gen path.
[01:40] Benji Rao: Okay. For sizing we need peak QPS, average, and burst profile shape. Any numbers?
[01:46] Priya Singh: Our baseline is 120 QPS average during business hours, concurrency roughly 30 live sessions — sessions produce bursts when a user clicks 'ask' quickly. We see bursts up to 300 QPS for short 20–30s windows during promotions.
[02:00] Maya Chen: Right, peak bursts are the hard thing. We want graceful degradation, not full fail. Fallback to cached search results or smaller model.
[02:08] Alice Park: This is where Redwood's routing and fallback policies come in — we can route to a cheaper quantized variant when load is high, and have region/priority based routing too.
[02:17] Rafael Ortiz: Quick question on our latency targets — are they realistic for hosted vs dedicated? We're open to dedicated if we need consistent tail latency.
[02:24] Benji Rao: Dedicated will give more predictable p99s; hosted can hit targets with autoscaling + prefix caching but tail behavior is more variable under extreme bursts. For your 300 QPS bursts, dedicated or reserved burst capacity is recommended.
[02:36] Maya Chen: What's the typical setup for a 2-week pilot? We don't want a heavy contract but need data to decide.
[02:42] Alice Park: For pilots we do a short reserved environment: Redwood can spin up a dedicated pool in your VPC (Private) or in our hosted but peered network. We use a replay harness to replay your anonymized traces and run benchmarks at various QPS points. Two-week window is fine.
[02:56] Priya Singh: Replay harness — what format? We use k6 and some custom scripts.
[03:00] Benji Rao: We provide example k6 scripts and a small replay tool. We ask for traces in JSONL with timestamps, input token counts, and a label for interactive vs search. If you can't share full traces we can do synthetic shaping from histograms.
[03:14] Rafael Ortiz: We can definitely export a week of anonymized traces. We'll need to scrub user IDs.
[03:19] Maya Chen: On success criteria — besides latency & cost, we want quality to be within delta of our baseline gen model. How do you measure quality regressions?
[03:28] Alice Park: We recommend a prompt set and eval harness — Redwood Optimize can run pairwise comparisons and surface regressions vs baseline prompts. For the POC we'll include a short eval set of ~150 prompts you can agree to.
[03:38] Rafael Ortiz: Good. We also need to see token accounting and cost breakdown per route, especially the embedding calls and any pre/post-processing tokenization differences.
[03:46] Benji Rao: We can produce token-level accounting per route and per API key — console has that. Note transcription — tokenization differences across model families can alter costs by ~5–10% sometimes; we'll call that out in the benchmark results.
[03:58] Priya Singh: Security: SSO with SAML? Audit logs? KMS?
[04:02] Alice Park: Yes to all: SAML for admin access, KMS integration for keys in Private, and audit logs shipped to your SIEM. We'll attach the SOC2 and our security runbook in the follow-up.
[04:11] Maya Chen: Competitors — our infra team previously benchmarked Anthropic on local endpoints, cost was higher but tail latency good. We want to compare apples-to-apples.
[04:20] Benji Rao: Understood. We'll include a comparable throughput-latency spreadsheet and guidance on model selection.
[04:25] Alice Park: About model selection — do you have a preferred open-model family or are you flexible?
[04:29] Rafael Ortiz: We're moving away from closed APIs, prefer open models. But for re-ranking we might keep a hosted vector provider.
[04:36] Benji Rao: Okay. For throughput math: if your average is 120 QPS with 30 concurrent sessions and 3–4 turns per session, your steady-state token throughput is roughly: (120 queries * average tokens per query). For gen path (~30% of traffic) with 160 tokens total (in+out), that's ~5,760 tokens/s for gen; search path is primarily low token calls. We'll put concrete arithmetic in the benchmark doc.
[04:58] Maya Chen: Do you support kv cache reuse across session? Because our assistant can get long dialogs.
[05:03] Benji Rao: Yes, Redwood runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; reusing cache will reduce token compute for long context but still is memory bound on the runtime. We'll note cache eviction semantics in the doc.
[05:13] Rafael Ortiz: For the pilot we want 3 phases: 1) run replay on a small dataset to calibrate 2) ramp up to steady load and inject bursts 3) run end-to-end mix and measure p95/p99/cost. Is that workable?
[05:23] Alice Park: That's exactly the approach we use. We'll propose specific QPS targets for each phase and a timeline.
[05:28] Priya Singh: Timeline — we can provide traces by next Tuesday (2026-08-18) if we prioritize. Then run pilot the week after? We want results before end of August.
[05:36] Alice Park: If you provide traces 8/18, we can turn around a benchmark plan and run a live replay starting 8/24 for two weeks — aiming to finish by 9/7. That meets your end-of-August-ish goal.
[05:46] Maya Chen: Sounds good. Questions on instrumentation — we want token-level and tail-latency alerts. Can Redwood push metrics to our Datadog?
[05:53] Benji Rao: Yes, metrics and traces can export to Datadog/Prometheus and we can attach x-trace ids to requests for correlation.
[05:59] Rafael Ortiz: One more: what's the expected variance in p99 when we move from hosted to dedicated? Ballpark numbers?
[06:05] Benji Rao: Ballpark: hosted p99 could vary by +/- 20–30% under bursty load depending on batching behavior; dedicated reduces that to +/- 5–10% typically. We'll include historical charts in the follow-up doc.
[06:16] Priya Singh: Okay. Any blockers from our side? Network peering approvals might take a week. We can also do a hosted but VPC peering later.
[06:26] Alice Park: That's fine. For immediate benchmarking we can use a hosted test env with IP allowlist while peering is setup.
[06:32] Maya Chen: On contract side — we want a short trial NDA addendum and not a full enterprise contract for pilot. Is that usual?
[06:38] Alice Park: Yes, we can do a pilot SOW and a short security addendum. I'll loop in our agreements team.
[06:44] (brief cross-talk)
[06:48] Benji Rao: Quick note on modeling: when we replay traces please include per-request token counts and a tag for 'gen' vs 'search' so we can route properly in the harness. If you can't, provide token histograms and we can synthesize.
[06:58] Rafael Ortiz: We'll do the export with tags.
[07:01] Maya Chen: Anything else we should cover?
[07:04] Alice Park: Let's recap next steps and owners.
